BaaS Bu ild -Pr ompts Pla ook Co pa ni to 01_BaaS_Architecture_and_Cost.md Purpo se: an d e ac t t an engineer or coding agent Cl aude Code, et c.) Each is sel cont ained: cont xt objec iv e, ack, eq uir ement s, del iv er abl es, accep ance crit eria. The yr or der ed he bui d p hases i n the ar hi ec tur e doc Ho w t use t his pla ybo Lo open decisions th ar tu do t se al s br an on he isol at ion model and cl oud choice. Wo pha pha dont ar he cont ol ane unt il one ojec runs hand end- o- end. Ea ch pr ompt umes he ea er ha ea he chit ec ur oc. he ele nt re re th th t so th ag t h as c t. Tr Wher comp onent al eady xis op en- sour ce os gREST Go rue, eal ime, St or age, pg gr aphql, Supa vis or pos gr es met a, ong) he pr ompt is about integr ating, configuring, and wiring t n t r ti t. th ar hi ec tur e doc sa s y ou ha e a di er enti at or PHA SE 0 F ounda tions Pr pt Mo no epo aC CI/ CD sk elet CONTEXT: We are building a Supabase-class BaaS (see architecture doc 13). This task sets up the repository, infrastructure-as-code, and CI/CD foundations everything else builds on. OBJECTIVE: Create the monorepo and infrastructure skeleton. STACK: Git monorepo (Turborepo or Nx). Terraform for cloud infra. Kubernetes (EKS on AWS, per 15). Helm for service packaging. GitHub Actions (or GitLab CI) for CI/CD. Docker for all services. REQUIREMENTS: Pr pt .2 Base P st gr es im age PHA SE 1 Singl -te na nt da ta ne RE T + uth ate Pr pt st gRES T int egr at io - Monorepo layout: /apps (studio, platform-api, orchestrator), /services (data-plane service configs/forks), /infra (terraform, helm), /packages (shared libs), /docker (base images). - Terraform modules for: VPC/networking, EKS cluster, S3 buckets, RDS or self-managed Postgres for the control plane, secrets store (AWS Secrets Manager/KMS), container registry. - A reproducible local dev environment (docker-compose) that mirrors prod services. - CI: lint, test, build, push images. CD: deploy to a staging cluster via Helm. - Environment separation: local / staging / prod with isolated state. DELIVERABLES: Repo structure, Terraform modules, base Dockerfiles, Helm chart scaffolds, CI/CD pipelines, README for bootstrapping. ACCEPTANCE: - `terraform apply` stands up a clean staging environment. - A trivial service deploys to staging via the pipeline. - `docker-compose up` runs the local stack. CONTEXT: Every tenant project runs a PostgreSQL with a fixed set of extensions, schemas, and roles (architecture doc 2, 4.1). This is the canonical DB image. OBJECTIVE: Build a hardened PostgreSQL 16 Docker image with all required extensions and a bootstrap migration that creates reserved schemas and roles. STACK: PostgreSQL 16; extensions: uuid-ossp, pgcrypto, pgjwt, pg_graphql, pgvector, postgis (optional flag), pg_cron, pg_net, pgmq, supabase_vault, pg_stat_statements, pgaudit. REQUIREMENTS: - Install/enable all extensions above (postgis behind a build flag for a lighter default). - Bootstrap migration creates reserved schemas: auth, storage, realtime, graphql, extensions, vault, plus public. - Create reserved roles: anon, authenticated, service_role, plus per-service internal roles, with correct grants. Default-deny on public objects. - Configure: sane connection limits, logical replication enabled (wal_level=logical) for Realtime, pg_stat_statements + pgaudit on. - Provide an idempotent migration runner. DELIVERABLES: Dockerfile, init/migration SQL, role/grant matrix doc, config (postgresql.conf overrides). ACCEPTANCE: - Container boots; `\\dx` lists all extensions; reserved schemas/roles exist. - A test confirms anon/authenticated/service_role behave correctly against an RLS-protected table. - Logical replication slot can be created. Pr pt .2 ut h ser vice ( Go rue) int egr at io Pr pt 3 API G at y ( ng) API k CONTEXT: Architecture doc 4.2, 6. PostgREST turns the Postgres schema into a REST API and relies on RLS for authorization. OBJECTIVE: Deploy and configure PostgREST against the base Postgres image, JWT-aware, RLS-enforcing. STACK: PostgREST (official image), the base Postgres from 0.2. REQUIREMENTS: - Configure PostgREST to read the JWT secret, map the `role` claim to the Postgres role, and expose claims via request.jwt.claims. - Expose schema `public`; RPC for Postgres functions at /rpc. - Stateless, horizontally scalable deployment (Helm). - Health/readiness probes. DELIVERABLES: Helm chart, config, example schema + RLS policies for testing. ACCEPTANCE: - An anon request only sees anon-permitted rows; an authenticated JWT sees its own rows per RLS using auth.uid(). - RPC endpoint executes a Postgres function. - Schema changes reflect in the API without redeploy. CONTEXT: Architecture doc 4.4. End-user auth INSIDE a tenant project. Issues JWT access tokens + refresh tokens; writes users to the auth schema. OBJECTIVE: Deploy and configure a GoTrue-class auth server wired to the project Postgres, issuing JWTs PostgREST/Realtime/Storage trust. STACK: GoTrue (use-as-is or light fork per 15), project Postgres, SMTP provider (stub now, real in Phase 7 email prompt). REQUIREMENTS: - Methods: email/password, magic link, phone OTP (provider-pluggable), OAuth (Google/GitHub at minimum), MFA (TOTP), anonymous sign-in. - Shared JWT secret with PostgREST/Realtime/Storage; correct claims (sub=user id, role=authenticated, etc.). - Refresh-token rotation; configurable token TTLs. - Trigger to mirror auth.users public.profiles. - SMTP config surface (templates for confirm/recovery/invite/email-change). DELIVERABLES: Helm chart, config, DB trigger, email-template set, provider config docs. ACCEPTANCE: - Full signup confirm login refresh flow works; JWT validates downstream and RLS sees auth.uid(). - One OAuth provider completes end-to-end. - TOTP MFA enrol + challenge works. Milest one 1 check A developer can: create a project DB by hand sign up a user via Auth receive a JWT CRUD their own rows via the gateway+PostgREST under RLS. PHA SE 2 R time Stor ge Pr pt ealt im e ser er CONTEXT: Architecture doc 4.10, 6, 8. Single public endpoint per project; routes to services; validates anon/service_role keys at the edge. OBJECTIVE: Stand up Kong as the per-project gateway with path routing and API-key validation. STACK: Kong, the services from 1.11.2 (Realtime/Storage/Functions added later). REQUIREMENTS: - Routes: /auth/v1/* Auth, /rest/v1/* PostgREST, /graphql/v1 GraphQL, /realtime/v1/* Realtime, /storage/v1/* Storage, /functions/v1/* Functions (wire the ones that exist; leave stubs). - Validate the anon key (public) and service_role key (secret) both signed JWTs carrying project ref + role; attach the JWT to upstream requests. - Rate limiting + CORS at the edge. - Per-project config templated by project ref/domain. DELIVERABLES: Kong declarative config (or DB-backed), Helm chart, key-generation utility. ACCEPTANCE: - A request with a valid anon key reaches PostgREST and respects RLS; an invalid key is rejected at the gateway. - service_role key bypasses RLS (server-side test only). - Routing works for all live services. CONTEXT: Architecture doc 4.5, 6, 9. WebSocket server for Postgres Changes (WAL subscribers, RLS-filtered), Broadcast, and Presence. OBJECTIVE: Deploy and configure the Elixir/Phoenix Realtime server against the project Postgres logical-replication slot. STACK: Realtime (official image), project Postgres (wal_level=logical from 0.2), shared JWT secret. REQUIREMENTS: - Postgres Changes via a replication slot + logical decoding; per-subscriber RLS filtering using the connection JWT. - Broadcast (ephemeral pub/sub) and Presence (online state) channels. - Auth handshake on WS connect using the JWT. - Horizontal clustering; per-tenant connection/slot limits (9). DELIVERABLES: Helm chart, config, client test harness (supabase-js or raw WS). Pr pt .2 age ser vice PHA SE 3 Functions + Gr hQL + ool Pr pt Edge Funct io ns runt im ACCEPTANCE: - An insert/update/delete on an RLS-protected table is pushed only to authorized subscribers. - Broadcast and Presence channels work between two clients. - Connection cap enforced. CONTEXT: Architecture doc 4.6, 6. Objects in S3/MinIO; metadata + access policies in Postgres (storage schema) governed by RLS; image transforms via imgproxy. OBJECTIVE: Deploy storage-api wired to S3 (MinIO locally) with Postgres-backed metadata and RLS access control. STACK: storage-api (official image), S3 (prod) / MinIO (local), imgproxy, project Postgres, shared JWT. REQUIREMENTS: - Buckets (public/private), object CRUD, signed URLs, resumable uploads (TUS). - Access governed by RLS on storage.buckets / storage.objects, consistent with DB auth. - On-the-fly image transforms via imgproxy. - Egress through CDN-friendly paths (cost 11). DELIVERABLES: Helm chart, config, S3/MinIO setup, RLS policy examples, client tests. ACCEPTANCE: - Upload/download/list/delete respect RLS for anon vs authenticated. - Signed URL grants temporary access; resumable upload of a large file succeeds. - Image transform returns a resized variant. CONTEXT: Architecture doc 4.7, 6. Deno-based serverless TypeScript per project; injected secrets; controlled egress. # iCloud Drive — Path to 100% Perfect Generated 2026-06-07 by Claude (6-agent parallel audit). Read top-to-bottom; ordered by impact. --- ## The one root problem: three competing naming schemes Your root mixes THREE systems. This is the single biggest thing to fix. 1. Numbered categories (the good system): `00 ⭐ IMPORTANT`, `01 Personal & Family` … `09 Organization` 2. Numbered projects: `001.SURYA AGENTIC`, `002.LocalAITV Project` 3. Loose orphans that break the scheme: `AI-Training`, `Codex`, `Desktop`, `Documents`, `new laptop desktop` **Recommendation:** Commit to ONE scheme. Keep `00–09`, and add a single `10 Projects/` that holds SURYA AGENTIC, LocalAITV, and Codex underneath it. Then no loose folders remain at root. Target root (12 items, nothing else): ``` 00 ⭐ IMPORTANT 01 Personal & Family 02 Work & Business 03 Finance & Bills 04 Travel 05 AI & Learning 06 Media 07 Health & Medical 08 Archive & Misc 09 Organization 10 Projects/ ← SURYA-AGENTIC, LocalAITV, Codex live here ``` --- ## PRIORITY 1 — Remove what should never be in iCloud (biggest space + sync win) These are re-creatable build artifacts silently eating your iCloud quota and slowing sync on every device: - `001.SURYA AGENTIC/build/` — ~37 MB build output - `002.LocalAITV Project/.../.git/` — active git repo (thousands of object files) - `new laptop desktop/Desktop/localaitv-submission-kit/capacitor-project/node_modules/` — reinstallable, huge - `new laptop desktop/Pictures/Photos Library.photoslibrary/` — a whole Photos library should NOT live in iCloud Drive **Action:** Delete these from iCloud. Code lives in git/GitHub; node_modules rebuilds with `npm install`; the Photos library belongs in the Photos app, not Drive. --- ## PRIORITY 2 — Eliminate the orphan root folders | Folder | Finding | Action | |---|---|---| | `AI-Training` | only empty `.keep` stubs | DELETE | | `Desktop` | only `.localized` + a `.claude` config | DELETE (accidental system-folder sync) | | `Documents` | only `.localized` | DELETE (accidental sync) | | `Codex` | real helpdesk + landing-page projects | MOVE → `10 Projects/Codex` | | `new laptop desktop` | full 2nd desktop + node_modules + Photos bloat | EXTRACT source → `10 Projects/`, then DELETE the rest | | `_DUPLICATES-BIN` | 17 verified copies (already deduped) | DELETE once you've glanced at it | --- ## PRIORITY 3 — De-duplicate inside the projects - `001.SURYA AGENTIC/Suryagentic_Complete_Package/` appears **3 times** — keep one. - `001.SURYA AGENTIC/Claude-Mastery-100h` vs `..._BACKUP-before-deepening` — contents DIFFER, so this is NOT a safe auto-delete; compare and keep the newer, delete the stale backup deliberately. - `002.LocalAITV Project` has overlapping `LocalAI` / `LocalAITV` folder variants and 60+ versioned docs in "Project Documents" — consolidate to one folder, keep latest of each doc. --- ## PRIORITY 4 — Filename hygiene (breaks "not a single improper file") Fix these classes wherever they appear: - **Doubled extensions:** `...BookingReceipt-376327 (1).pdf.pdf`, `IMG_0002.pdf.pdf`, `Screenshot ....jpeg.png` → strip the second extension. - **Trailing space before extension:** `Dad Dubai visa .pdf`, `China application form .pdf`, `hasika report .pdf` → remove the space. - **Cryptic / machine names:** `CEACAA00CZW8VX.PDF` (×4), `000.pdf`, `1680473381.pdf`, `50026696911419.pdf`, `generic_621536185.pdf` → rename to what they actually are (e.g. "USA-DS160-confirmation.pdf"). - **macOS auto-copies:** ` 2`, ` 3`, `(1)`, `(5)` suffixes → verify then delete the copy. - **No-extension file:** `Screenshot 2026-06-05 at 3.46.51 PM` (Media/Screenshots) → add `.png` or remove if corrupt. - **Burst series:** `PHOTO-2024-09-22-10-13-06` variants 2–9 → keep the best 1–2. --- ## PRIORITY 5 — Verify financial/legal docs are NOT lost as "duplicates" These look like copies by name but are almost certainly DISTINCT records — do **not** auto-delete: - `03 Finance & Bills/AnnuityPaidCertificate` (base + 2–7) → likely different years - `03 Finance & Bills/Statement_MAR2024_661111578` (base + 2–5) → bank statements - Everything under `00 ⭐ IMPORTANT` (passports, LIC, PAN, Aadhaar, property) → leave alone; review by hand only. --- ## PRIORITY 6 — Tidy the meta-folder `09 Organization` holds ~23 prior audit logs, scripts, and reports (`_CLEANUP-*`, `_AUDIT-*`, `.sh` scripts, `_tree.json`, several HTML reports). Useful history, but redundant. **Recommendation:** keep the latest 2–3 (this file + one tree map) and move the rest into `09 Organization/_archive-logs/`. --- ## ⚠️ Important caveat: cloud-only files During this audit, several folders (`00 ⭐ IMPORTANT`, `01 Personal & Family`, `02 Work & Business`, `03 Finance`, `05 AI & Learning`, `07 Health & Medical`) read as empty to the scanners. They are not empty — their contents are **stored in iCloud only and not downloaded** to this Mac, so tools can't see or safely rename them. To let me (or you) clean those folders, in Finder: right-click each → **"Download Now"** (or System Settings → Apple ID → iCloud → turn OFF "Optimize Mac Storage" temporarily). Once downloaded, I can run filename fixes and dedup across them too. --- ## Suggested execution order 1. You: download the cloud-only folders (above) so nothing is hidden. 2. Me: delete Priority-1 bloat + Priority-2 orphans (to a recoverable bin first). 3. Me: dedupe projects (P3) and fix filenames (P4) with content verification. 4. You: hand-review P5 financial/identity items. 5. Me: tidy `09 Organization` (P6). Tell me "do priorities 1–4" and I'll execute the safe, reversible ones now.

# SURYA-AGENTIC — Surya Intel / training business - 01 Training Courses — Claude Mastery course, complete packages, catalogs & manuals - "Claude-Mastery-100h-REVISED-wip" = NEW EDITION BEING BUILT right now (work in progress — leave it alone until finished) - 02 Websites — Surya Agentic + Surya Intel website files - 03 Institute — Surya Agentic Institute (course content, marketing images) - 04 Business Documents — products & services docs, handoffs, SURYA INTEL business unit (real estate, hospitals, equity) - 05 Old & Backup Files — old versions; two Claude-Mastery backup editions are zipped here

# Pilot kit — validate the manual with 3 real learners in one week The manual's last unverified claims are its **time labels** and its **self-teachability**. Only real learners can verify those. This kit runs that test with minimal effort. ## Who to recruit (3 people, one per track) - **A (App track):** a non-technical professional who has used ChatGPT/Claude casually. - **B (Builder track):** someone who has written some Python but never called an API. - **C (Operator track):** a developer who lives in a terminal but hasn't used Claude Code. Each pilots a different slice: A → Modules 0.0–0.3 + 1.1–1.4. B → 0.0, 0.2, 4.1–4.4. C → 0.0, 0.2, 6.1–6.4. (~6 modules each ≈ one week at 1 module/evening.) ## What each learner records (the friction log) One spreadsheet row per module: | Column | What to write | |---|---| | Module | e.g. 4.2 | | Start/end time | wall-clock, honest | | Stuck points | anything that took >5 min to get past, with the sentence/step that caused it | | Mismatch | any place the book said X but the product showed Y | | Practice result | did the Practice succeed against its criteria? consulted the model solution? | | Quiz score | (end of slice) score on that part's checkpoint quiz | | One-line verdict | "clear / confusing because… / brilliant because…" | ## Pass criteria for the manual (not the learner) 1. **Time honesty:** median actual time within ±40% of the header estimate for ≥4 of 6 modules. 2. **Self-sufficiency:** learner completes ≥5 of 6 modules without external help (web searches about the *product* count as failures of the book; searches about their own OS don't). 3. **Practice executability:** ≥80% of attempted practices succeed against their stated criteria. 4. **Mismatch count:** <2 product-mismatch reports per learner (each one becomes an errata row). ## After the week (2 hours of your time) 1. Collect the three logs; copy every Stuck point and Mismatch into `ERRATA.md` in the sources root. 2. Re-time any module that breached the ±40% band; update its header label. 3. Fix the top 5 stuck points in the sources (usually one sentence each); rebuild (`build.py`, `html_build.py`, `qa.py`). 4. Add one line to the edition note: "Pilot-tested with N learners, <month year>." That last line — earned, not asserted — is what separates a world-class manual from a merely correct one.

# Claude Mastery — The Daily Course **120 minutes a day, every session hands-on, until mastery — built from the revised & verified manual (June 2026).** *Suryagentic Institute · catalog edition* --- ## How this course works **The contract.** One session = 120 focused minutes. Every session ends with something that exists — a working chat technique, a file, a script, an agent, a passed quiz. No session is theory-only; the manual's golden rule (build first, name the concept second) is enforced by the schedule itself. **The rhythm of every session (the 10/95/15 shape).** | Minutes | What happens | |---|---| | 0:00–0:10 | **Retrieval warm-up** — answer yesterday's three recall questions from memory, then check. (Spaced retrieval is the single best-evidenced learning intervention; it's built into every day, not just quiz days.) | | 0:10–1:45 | **The work** — the day's module(s): read a section, DO THIS with your own hands, hit the practices, compare against the model solution. The session plans below tell you where the time goes. | | 1:45–2:00 | **Close the loop** — tick the module checkpoint, write one line in your wins file, write tomorrow's three recall questions, preview tomorrow's title. | **Cadence.** Daily is the design (Mon–Sat with Sunday off works beautifully; 5 days/week just makes the course ~20% longer in calendar time). Never do two sessions back-to-back to "catch up" — retention, not speed, is the metric. **Materials.** The manual (PDF or HTML edition), the Companion Code repo, a wins file (Module 0.3 sets it up), and from Part 4 onward: a terminal, Python 3.10+, and an Anthropic API key with a spending cap (Module 4.1 — total course API spend stays under ₹2,000 if you follow the cheap-model defaults). **Three tracks.** This catalog lists the full course. App-track learners stop after Day 31 (Parts 0–3 + safety); Operator-track learners jump from Day 30 to the Part 6 block; Builder-track learners may skim Part 2. The placement guide (Module 0.0, Day 1) routes you. **Assessment.** Nine checkpoint quizzes with answer keys (one per part, each with a spaced-review section reaching back), model solutions for every first practice, and three capstones graded against the graduation rubric. Pass bar: 10/12 on quizzes, all-Pass on the rubric. --- ## PART 0 — Orientation *By the end of this part you are oriented: accounts live on every surface, the five-lands map memorised, study system installed.* ### Day 1 — What is Claude? # Resume Tailoring Guide — AI Agent Engineer (22-year senior pivot) The resume template (`AI-Agent-Engineer-Resume.docx`) ships with your AI sections fully written and your career history as **orange-bracketed placeholders** — fill those with real facts only. Never submit with a placeholder still visible. ## The positioning (why the resume is shaped this way) A 22-year engineer pivoting into AI has one advantage juniors can't copy: **production judgment**. The resume leads with the AI specialisation but anchors every AI claim in engineering discipline (evals, gates, cost, failure-safety). Don't bury your seniority — it's the differentiator, not baggage. One rule above all: **every AI bullet must stay true** — the capstone bullets become true the day you finish Days 85–107 of the course; don't send this resume before then. ## Filling the placeholders (45 minutes) 1. **Name/contact:** create a clean GitHub handle and LinkedIn slug now if yours are messy — they're part of the product. 2. **Engineering foundation cell:** your real stack. Keep it to 4 lines; 22 years compresses, it doesn't enumerate. 3. **Experience bullets:** Action → Scale → Result with a number. "Owned payments platform (₹X Cr/day); reduced incident rate 60%" beats three sentences of duties. Three detailed roles max; everything older is one line. 4. **The AI-adoption bullet** in your current role: only if truthful — and after Part 6 of the course it easily can be ("introduced Claude Code-based review workflow…"). 5. **[N] hrs/week in Capstone B bullet:** measure it during the build week; real numbers interview better than round ones. ## Per-market adjustments **Remote US / global (start here):** keep as-is (US Letter, no photo, no DOB). Sprinkle the exact phrase "AI agents" and "LLM" in the Profile — recruiters keyword-search those. Salary expectation: discuss in calls, never on paper. **India (GCCs/startups):** identical content; add a "Notice period: X days" line under contact. GCC recruiters scan for cloud + domain keywords — make the foundation cell carry them. **Gulf (UAE/Saudi):** identical (modern Gulf tech hiring is photo-free international format despite old advice). Add "Open to relocation — visa-eligible under UAE AI specialist routes" in the contact line. **Europe (DE/NL/UK):** add a one-line "Languages: English (fluent), [others]" row in Education. UK: change spelling to -ise forms (already done). NL/DE: month-precision dates on roles. ## ATS keyword checklist (the resume already contains the bold ones) **AI agents, LLM, Claude API, MCP (Model Context Protocol), agent orchestration, prompt engineering, RAG, embeddings, LLM evaluation, red-teaming, prompt injection, Claude Code, CI/CD**, plus add from your own history: Python, AWS/Azure/GCP, Docker, Kubernetes, microservices, SQL. If a job ad repeats a term three times, mirror it once in your Profile line. ## The companion assets (what actually gets you interviews) The resume opens doors only alongside: (1) **GitHub** — three capstone repos, each with README, eval printout screenshot, 30-second demo GIF; pin them. (2) **LinkedIn** — headline "AI Agent Engineer | 22y software engineering | Claude API · MCP · evals"; 4–6 posts written during the course (the Writing section links them). (3) **The 5-minute demo** — rehearsed, recorded as backup. Interviews for agent roles are increasingly "show me" — Capstone A *is* the standard interview question ("design a support agent with safety gates"), and you'll have built it. ## Sequence Finish course → fill placeholders same week → publish repos + 2 posts → apply remote-US + India GCC simultaneously (highest hit-rate pair) → use first interviews as rehearsal for Gulf/EU applications.

--- name: suryagentic-session-builder description: >- Build Suryagentic Institute teaching sessions — a word-for-word teleprompter SCRIPT plus a matching 16:9 SLIDE deck — in the exact format of the "Future Agentic Engineering" Session 1 reference. Use whenever the user wants to create, draft, or prepare material for an upcoming session of a Suryagentic course: e.g. "build Session 2", "make the script and slides for the next session", "prepare tonight's class material", "turn this material into a session", "write the session N script". The user supplies raw source content for one session; this skill distills it, maps it onto the standard session arc, writes the plain-language word-for-word script (black spoken text, gold [stage directions], navy "▶ SHOW SLIDE N" banners + timecodes), and produces a synced slide deck in the house visual style (navy/gold, analogy-driven diagrams). Produces two synced artifacts that match Session 1 exactly. --- # Suryagentic Session Builder Turn raw source material for one course session into the **two synced deliverables** Suryagentic Institute ships for every live class: 1. **A word-for-word teleprompter script** (PDF/Doc) — every word the presenter says, with gold `[stage directions]`, navy `▶ SHOW SLIDE N` advance-cues, and timecodes. 2. **A matching slide deck** (16:9) — clean, analogy-driven, navy-and-gold, one idea per slide. The gold standard both must match is the bundled **Session 1 — "Future Agentic Engineering" Course Overview** (`assets/reference-session-1/`). When in doubt, copy how Session 1 did it. --- ## When to use this skill Use it when the user asks to build, draft, or prepare a **session** (script and/or slides) for a Suryagentic course — "build Session 2", "prepare the next class", "turn this into a session", "write tonight's script and slides". **It expects raw source material for ONE session** (a manual module, an outline, notes, a topic + goals). If the user hasn't provided it yet, ask for it (see Intake below). Not for: general document writing, non-Suryagentic decks, or editing the manual itself. --- ## The one procedure: follow the workflow **`references/generation-workflow.md` is the master, step-by-step procedure.** Read it and follow it in order. In brief: 0. **Intake** — capture course, session #, topic, audience (+ any background bridge, e.g. SAP), duration, learning goals, and the source material. 1. **Distill** the source into 4–8 teachable ideas (≈ one idea per concept slide). 2. **Map** the ideas onto the session arc → draft the slide list using `templates/slide-outline-template.md`. 3. **Choose an everyday analogy** for each idea (and an SAP/enterprise bridge if the audience warrants), using the analogy library in `references/voice-and-language-rules.md`. 4. **Write the script** against the slides using `templates/script-template.md` — insert `▶ SHOW SLIDE N` banners, timecodes that sum to the duration, gold `[stage directions]`, and a chat-poll every 1–2 slides per `references/engagement-and-interaction.md`. 5. **Build the deck** to `references/slide-design-system.md` using `assets/slide-build-recipe.md`. 6. **Sync-check** — every `▶ SHOW SLIDE N` equals deck page N; titles match; timecodes are monotonic and sum to the session length. 7. **QA gate** — run the checklist in the workflow (voice, analogy-per-concept, words-per-slide, engagement cadence, memorable line, honesty beat, recap-before-advance, forward preview, quick-reference index, redaction). --- ## Intake — ask for these if missing - **Course** (default: "Future Agentic Engineering") and **Institute line** ("Suryagentic Institute · Hyderabad") - **Session number and title** - **Audience** and any background to bridge from (Session 1 bridges to **SAP / enterprise systems**) - **Duration** (Session 1 = 90 min) and **session type** (overview vs hands-on build) - **Learning goals** (what the learner can do by the end) - **The source material** for this session --- ## File map | File | What it's for | |---|---| | `references/generation-workflow.md` | **START HERE.** The end-to-end build procedure + QA gate. | | `references/session-blueprint.md` | The reusable narrative arc + timing model (how to lay out the slides/minutes). | | `references/voice-and-language-rules.md` | The plain-warm voice + the **analogy library** + the SAP bridge technique. | | `references/engagement-and-interaction.md` | The chat-poll cadence, stage-direction vocabulary, gestures, Q&A. | | `references/script-style-guide.md` | Exactly how the word-for-word script is constructed (the 3-layer text system, furniture). | | `references/slide-design-system.md` | **Source of truth for visual tokens** — palette, type, layout, diagram patterns. | | `references/example-session1-annotated.md` | The gold-standard worked example, slide by slide, with "why this works". | | `templates/script-template.md` | Fill-in-the-blank word-for-word script template. | | `templates/slide-outline-template.md` | Per-slide planning template (plan the deck before writing the script). | | `assets/slide-build-recipe.md` | How to actually produce the deck (pptx skill or HTML→PDF) in the house style. | | `assets/reference-session-1/` | The canonical Session 1 script + 16 slide images (+ source PDFs) to imitate. | --- ## House rules (non-negotiable — this is what makes it "Suryagentic") - **Plain, warm, beginner-first.** Grade 6–8 reading level. Second person. Short sentences. Contractions. - **Analogy first, then the technical point.** Every concept gets an everyday analogy (Maps-vs-driver, kitchen, new-hire ladder…) *before* the term. - **Bridge to the audience's world.** For this cohort, tie concepts to SAP / approvals / process / go-live. - **A chat check every 1–2 slides.** "Type YES if…", "type the number…", re-energisers before long stretches. - **One memorable line per big concept** ("a chatbot talks — an agent does"). - **Honesty beats** wherever outcomes/jobs come up ("no course can promise a job"). - **Recap-before-advance** at least once; **forward preview** near the end. - **Script ↔ slides are locked:** `▶ SHOW SLIDE N` == deck page N, titles match, timecodes sum to the duration. - **Minimal words on slides** (~≤25); prefer a diagram over bullets. - **Redact** presenter name and any keys/personal info before shipping. --- ## Visual signature (see `references/slide-design-system.md` for exact tokens) - 16:9. Navy text `#1A1F4E`, gold accent `#E8A020` (top bar + title underline), indigo diagram boxes `#3D3FB5` on lavender fill `#E8EAFF`, cream emphasis panels, gray sub-text. - Title underlined in gold; thin gold bar across the top of every slide; footer "Suryagentic Institute · Future Agentic Engineering" + page number. - Signature diagrams: two-column compare, 4-box anatomy, 3-step ladder, uphill journey path, outcomes grid. --- ## Output location Save each new session's deliverables next to the reference, e.g. `…/Suryagentic-Session-Builder/output/Session-<N>/` containing `Session<N>-Script.(md|pdf)` and `Session<N>-Slides.(pptx|pdf)`. Keep the script filename and the deck in sync. ## Quick start > "Here's the source material for Session 2 (…)". → Run `references/generation-workflow.md` from Step 0.

# How Session 1 Was Built — the format, decoded A deep read of the two reference files — *Session 1 Word-for-Word Script* (12 pp) and *Session 1 Slides* (16 slides) — for "Future Agentic Engineering" (Suryagentic Institute · Hyderabad). This is the pattern every future session will follow. Everything below is reverse-engineered from the actual files; the reusable machinery lives in this same folder (see the file map at the end). --- ## 1. The big idea: two artifacts, locked together A session is **two synced files**: 1. **A word-for-word teleprompter script** — literally every word the presenter says, read from an iPad while screen-sharing the deck. 2. **A 16:9 slide deck** — clean, mostly visual, one idea per slide. They are bound by a single rule: **`▶ SHOW SLIDE N` in the script == page N in the deck.** The script even opens with a "How to use this with the slides" page that teaches the presenter the cue system. --- ## 2. The script's three-layer text system Every line in the script is one of three layers, visually distinguished: | Layer | Looks like | Meaning | |---|---|---| | **Spoken** | black text | Say this, word for word. | | **Stage direction** | gold `[ in brackets ]` | Do this silently — *don't read aloud* (pause, smile, be on camera, check chat, point to a box). | | **Slide cue** | navy banner `▶ SHOW SLIDE N — Title` | Advance the deck to page N now. Followed by `( click your slides forward to page N now · 0:06–0:16 )` timecodes. | Page furniture is consistent: a header (`Session 1 — Word-for-Word Script | Syncs with the slide deck`), a footer (`Read the black text · the gold [brackets] are directions · Page X`), and a closing **"Quick reference — the 16 slides"** index listing each slide with its start time. **Two delivery tips are stated up front:** (1) speak slower and warmer than feels natural; (2) deliver the examples like little stories and pause after each — *"the goal isn't to sound clever; it's to make every single person think 'oh, NOW I get it.'"* That sentence is the design philosophy of the whole format. --- ## 3. The 16-slide arc (and the minute budget) A repeatable narrative spine for a 90-minute overview: | # | Slide | Starts | Beat / function | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | Title — welcome | 0:00 | Warm cold-open + chat warm-up | | 2 | What we'll cover | 0:03 | Agenda — "nothing scary" | | 3 | What IS an agent? | 0:06 | **Define the core concept** (longest teaching beat) | | 4 | Anatomy of an agent | 0:16 | Mental model — the 4 parts | | 5 | Why now? | 0:26 | Motivation + opportunity | | 6 | The Ladder | 0:34 | **The one key framework** | | 7 | Your journey (7 parts, 26 sessions) | 0:45 | Roadmap, drawn as an uphill path | | 8–11 | Parts 1&2 / 3&4 / 5&6 / 7+Capstone | 0:49–1:12 | Walk the roadmap | | 12 | What you walk away with | 1:17 | Outcomes & proof (portfolio) | | 13 | How the course works | 1:23 | Logistics | | 14 | What you need | 1:26 | Logistics | | 15 | Your first step | 1:28 | Call to action | | 16 | Thank you + Q&A | 1:29 | Close | The heavy teaching minutes go to slides **3, 4, and 6** (concept, mental model, framework). Everything after slide 7 is short. This budget rescales for 60/120-min sessions (see `references/session-blueprint.md`). --- ## 4. The teaching engine (why it lands) Repeatable rhetorical machinery, used on nearly every slide: - **Analogy first, then the technical point.** Every concept opens with an everyday picture, *then* names the idea. The full set used in Session 1: chatbot vs **Google Maps vs a driver**; **recipe site vs a personal chef**; the **angry "where's my order?" email**; the **kitchen** = the 4-part anatomy (order→chef→tools→dish); the **new hire** = the ladder; an **open-book exam** = looking things up in your documents; a **waiter who remembers your usual** = agent memory. - **Bridge to the audience's world.** This cohort is ex-**SAP / enterprise**, so concepts are tied to approval workflows, end-to-end process, and "the care you take before a production go-live." That experience is reframed as a *head start*, not a gap. - **Two reusable mental models** the whole course leans on: - **Anatomy = Trigger → Brain → Tools → Output** ("every agent is just these four parts"). - **The Ladder = Prompt → Context → Harness** (instructions → the right information → the checks, limits, and memory around it). "The right info beats more info." - **One memorable line per concept** — *"a chatbot talks — an agent does."* / *"proof beats promises."* - **Honesty beats.** Whenever jobs/outcomes come up: *"no course can promise you a job… what I CAN promise is real skills and real proof."* This builds trust and is a fixed move, not a throwaway. - **Constant reassurance** — "nothing scary", "you'll never feel lost", "nobody gets left behind." - **Recap-before-advance** (slide 7 pauses to restate the two big ideas before the roadmap) and a **forward preview** at the close. --- ## 5. The engagement rhythm Participation is engineered, not improvised: - **Opening warm-up:** "type the number **1** if you can see my screen and hear me." (Confirms tech + gets the first easy action.) - **A chat check every 1–2 slides** — comprehension checks ("type YES if the difference makes sense"), personal ones ("has anyone been asked about AI at work?"), and **re-energisers** before long stretches and the home stretch ("which would save YOU the most time…"). - **Stage-direction vocabulary:** *Let it land · Wait, and warmly acknowledge a few · React warmly · Read a few answers aloud.* - **Physical gestures:** *point to each box · run your finger up the three steps · be on camera / come back on camera.* - **Q&A close:** read each question aloud, "no question is too small," and a seeded question if it's quiet. --- ## 6. The slide visual system - **16:9**, very low text density (one idea per slide, diagram over bullets). - **Palette:** navy `#1A1F4E` (all text), gold/amber `#E8A020` (thin top bar + the underline under each title), indigo `#3D3FB5` boxes on lavender `#E8EAFF` fills, cream emphasis panels, gray sub-text. - **Furniture:** gold bar across the top; title with a gold underline; footer "Suryagentic Institute · Future Agentic Engineering" + page number. - **Signature diagrams:** two-column compare (chatbot vs agent), a 4-box anatomy row with arrows, a 3-rung ladder with a "climb" arrow, an uphill dotted journey path from "YOU, today" to "Job-ready!", and an outcomes/portfolio grid. Exact tokens: `references/slide-design-system.md`. --- ## 7. How future sessions get built (the reusable system) This folder is a **skill** that reproduces all of the above on demand. You hand over the source material for a session; it distills it, lays it on the arc, writes the script in this voice with the cue/timecode furniture, and builds a matching deck in the house style — then runs a sync-check and QA gate. | File | Purpose | |---|---| | `SKILL.md` | Entry point / orchestration. | | `references/generation-workflow.md` | The step-by-step build procedure + QA gate. | | `references/session-blueprint.md` | The arc + minute budget (and 60/120-min rescaling). | | `references/voice-and-language-rules.md` | The voice + the full analogy library + the SAP bridge. | | `references/engagement-and-interaction.md` | The chat-poll cadence, gestures, Q&A. | | `references/script-style-guide.md` | How the script is constructed (the 3-layer system, furniture). | | `references/slide-design-system.md` | Visual tokens + diagram patterns (source of truth). | | `references/example-session1-annotated.md` | Session 1 walked slide-by-slide with "why it works". | | `templates/script-template.md` | Fill-in-the-blank script. | | `templates/slide-outline-template.md` | Per-slide planning grid. | | `assets/slide-build-recipe.md` | How to render the deck in-style. | | `assets/reference-session-1/` | The original Session 1 script + 16 slide images to imitate. | **Next step:** hand over the source material for the next session and say "build it" — the skill takes it from there.

# Suryagentic Institute — Slide Visual Design System ## Reference: Session 1 "Future Agentic Engineering — Course Overview" (16 slides, 1834×1032) --- ## 1. Canvas & Aspect Ratio | Property | Value | |---|---| | Pixel dimensions | 1834 × 1032 px | | Aspect ratio | 16:9 | | Orientation | Landscape | | Background | Pure white `#FFFFFF` | --- ## 2. Color Palette All colors sampled directly from the slide images. | Role | Hex | Where used | |---|---|---| | **Navy / Primary Text** | `#1A1F4E` | All headings, slide titles, body bold text, diagram box labels, footer text | | **Gold / Accent** | `#E8A020` | Top header bar, title-slide gold rule underline, closing-slide rule, bullet dots, ladder step 3 box border + numeral, journey path capstone dot, star icon on slide 12, "Job-ready!" label | | **Indigo / Diagram Blue** | `#3D3FB5` | Agent diagram boxes (slide 3), anatomy boxes TRIGGER / BRAIN / OUTPUT (slide 4), journey path dots (slides 7, 8–11 part boxes), portfolio grid box borders (slide 12), part-card box borders (slides 8–11), upward arrows in diagrams | | **Lavender / Diagram Fill** | `#E8EAFF` | Interior fill of Agent panel (slide 3), anatomy box fills, part-card interior backgrounds (slides 8–11) | | **Warm Cream / Highlight Fill** | `#FFF5E0` | Chatbot panel fill (slide 3), Capstone box fill (slide 12) | | **Subtitle / Muted Text** | `#6B7280` | Subtitle text on title slide, muted sub-labels, footer (lighter rendering) | | **Gold Amber (lighter)** | `#F0B030` | Top accent bar (the full-width bar — slightly lighter amber) | | **Gray Line / Path** | `#C0C0C8` | Journey path connecting line (slide 7), box rule underlines on content slides | | **White** | `#FFFFFF` | Slide background, text inside filled navy boxes | > **Usage rule:** Navy is always the dominant ink color. Gold is strictly an accent — used for one element per slide at most. Indigo is reserved for interactive/diagram elements only; never used for body prose. --- ## 3. Typography ### Font Family The typeface throughout is a **humanist sans-serif** — visually identical to **Nunito** or a close variant (rounded terminals, open apertures, slightly condensed weight at large sizes). No serif fonts appear anywhere. No monospace except inside diagram "tool" labels. ### Type Scale (relative to 1834×1032 canvas) | Role | Approx px (at canvas res) | Weight | Case | Color | |---|---|---|---|---| | **Cover title** (slide 1 only) | ~96–100 px | ExtraBold / 800 | Title case | `#1A1F4E` | | **Cover subtitle** ("Course Overview — Session 1") | ~52 px | Bold / 700 | Title case | `#1A1F4E` | | **Cover tagline** | ~36 px | Regular / 400 | Sentence case | `#6B7280` | | **Slide title** (slides 2–16) | ~62–68 px | Bold / 700 | Sentence case (first word cap) | `#1A1F4E` | | **Slide sub-heading / intro line** | ~28–30 px | Regular / 400 | Sentence case | `#6B7280` | | **Bullet primary** (bold label) | ~34–36 px | Bold / 700 | Sentence case | `#1A1F4E` | | **Bullet secondary** (sub-text) | ~26–28 px | Regular / 400 | Sentence case | `#6B7280` | | **Diagram box label** | ~28–34 px | Bold / 700 | ALL CAPS | `#1A1F4E` or `#3D3FB5` | | **Diagram caption / sub-label** | ~22–24 px | Regular / 400 | Sentence case | `#1A1F4E` | | **Callout / analogy line** (bold bottom line) | ~28–32 px | Bold / 700 | Sentence case | `#1A1F4E` or `#3D3FB5` | | **Footer** | ~20 px | Regular / 400 | Mixed | `#9CA3AF` (very muted) | | **Slide number** | ~20 px | Regular / 400 | Numeric | `#9CA3AF` | | **Part-card title** (slides 8–11) | ~28–30 px | Bold / 700 | Title case | `#3D3FB5` | | **"Learn:" / "Build:" key** | ~24–26 px | Bold / 700 | Title case | `#1A1F4E` | ### Typography Rules - Line-height: generous (~1.4–1.5) — text never feels cramped - Letter-spacing: slightly open on headings; default on body - No italic used anywhere in the 16 slides - No underline decoration (except the gold rule, which is a graphic element, not text underline) - Bullet primary + secondary always appear as a pair; blank line between pairs --- ## 4. Layout Grid & Margins ### Global Margins (approximate, at 1834×1032) | Zone | Size | |---|---| | Top safe area (below accent bar) | ~80–90 px | | Left margin | ~80–90 px | | Right margin | ~80–90 px | | Bottom safe area (above footer) | ~70–80 px | | Accent bar height (top) | ~18–22 px | ### Grid - **Single-column** content area used for title slides, bullet slides, and closing slides. - **Two-column** layout used for slide 3 (Chatbot vs Agent) only — columns are roughly equal width with a clear gutter (~60 px). - **Horizontal flow** (left-to-right connected boxes) used for slide 4 (anatomy chain). - **Vertical stack with left axis** used for slide 6 (ladder). - **Diagonal path** used for slide 7 (journey roadmap) — no formal grid. - **Stacked cards** (full-width cards, top-to-bottom with gap) used for slides 8–11. - **Mixed grid + flow** used for slide 12 (portfolio grid left, capstone flow right). ### Title Placement - Slide title: top-left, immediately below top accent bar, left-aligned. - Gold rule: a thin horizontal line (~3–4 px, gold `#E8A020`) directly below the slide title text, spanning approximately 40–50% of title text width (not full-width). - Sub-heading / intro line: immediately below gold rule, left-aligned. - Content body: begins ~40–60 px below the intro line. --- ## 5. Accent Bar (Top Header) - **Full-width** horizontal bar at very top of every slide. - Height: ~18–22 px. - Color: `#F0B030` (gold-amber). - No text inside the bar. - Appears on ALL 16 slides including title (slide 1) and closing (slide 16). --- ## 6. Footer - Appears on all slides. - Bottom-left: `Suryagentic Institute · Future Agentic Engineering` — muted gray, small (~20 px), regular weight. - Bottom-right: slide number only (e.g., `02`), same size/color. - No logo mark or icon in footer. - Footer sits inside the bottom safe area; no rule/line above it. > **PERSONALIZATION FLAG:** The footer text "Suryagentic Institute · Future Agentic Engineering" and the slide number are the only elements that must be updated per-course. The presenter name does NOT appear in any slide (it is implied by "with me" on slide 13). No headshot or presenter name is shown — safe to leave as-is. --- ## 7. Bullet Pattern (slides 2, 5, 13, 14, 15) - Gold filled circle `●` bullet dot (~14–16 px diameter), color `#E8A020`. - **Primary line**: bold, navy, ~34–36 px — the headline of the point. - **Secondary line**: regular, muted gray, ~26–28 px — one supporting clause directly below primary; indented to align with primary text (not with bullet dot). - Maximum 4 bullet pairs per slide. - No sub-sub bullets. - No numbered lists. - Approximate max words per slide: **60–80 words** (title + intro + 4 bullet pairs). --- ## 8. Diagram Patterns — Detailed Specifications ### Slide 3 — Two-Column Compare (Chatbot vs Agent) - Two large rounded-rectangle panels, side by side, equal width, equal height. - **Left panel (Chatbot):** fill `#FFF5E0` (warm cream), border `#C0C0C8` (light gray ~2 px), rounded corners (~16 px radius). - Top label: "CHATBOT" — Bold, ALL CAPS, navy `#1A1F4E`, ~36 px. - Inner box: rounded rect with gray border, text "how can I help?" in quotes, regular navy. - Bottom label: "only TALKS" — Bold, navy. Sub: "answers, but can't act" — regular, muted. - **Right panel (Agent):** fill `#E8EAFF` (lavender), border `#3D3FB5` (indigo, ~2–3 px), rounded corners (~16 px). - Top label: "AGENT" — Bold, ALL CAPS, indigo `#3D3FB5`, ~36 px. - Inner structure: output speech bubble ("done — I've handled it"), then three indigo-bordered tool boxes (EMAIL / SHEET / CAL) arranged horizontally with indigo arrows pointing up from tools to speech bubble. - Bottom label: "TALKS + DOES" — Bold, indigo. Sub: "takes real action in the world" — regular, navy. - **Bottom callout** (below both panels, centered): bold navy italic-style text — "Like this: a chatbot tells you 'how to do it.' An agent just goes and does it." - Gutter between panels: ~60 px. ### Slide 4 — Four-Box Horizontal Flow (Anatomy) - Four equal-width boxes in a horizontal left-to-right chain. - Boxes: rounded rectangles (~16 px radius), ~220 px wide × ~120 px tall. - **Box fills/borders:** TRIGGER = lavender fill + indigo border; BRAIN = lavender fill + indigo border; TOOLS = white fill + gold border (`#E8A020`); OUTPUT = lavender fill + indigo border. - **Label**: ALL CAPS Bold, ~30 px, navy inside box. - **Sub-label**: regular ~22 px, muted gray, below label inside box. - **Arrows**: solid indigo filled triangular arrowheads (`▶`) between each box, ~30 px. - Below chain: centered regular text "Every agent you build has these four parts." - Bottom callout: bold navy "Like a kitchen: an order comes in, the chef decides, uses tools, and plates the dish." - Chain is horizontally centered in the content area. ### Slide 6 — Three-Step Vertical Ladder (Prompt / Context / Harness) - Vertical arrow (navy/indigo, solid, pointing upward) on the left side, labeled "climb" in small regular navy. - Three stacked horizontal pill-boxes (wide, ~600 px wide × ~90 px tall), left-aligned to the arrow, bottom to top: PROMPT (1), CONTEXT (2), HARNESS (3). - **Box styling:** - PROMPT: white fill, gray border (`#C0C0C8`), navy bold label ALL CAPS, muted sub-text. Numeral "1" right-aligned inside box, navy. - CONTEXT: lavender fill (`#E8EAFF`), indigo border (`#3D3FB5`), indigo bold label ALL CAPS. Numeral "2" right-aligned, indigo. - HARNESS: white fill, gold border (`#E8A020`), navy bold label ALL CAPS. Numeral "3" right-aligned, gold. - Stacking order: PROMPT at bottom, HARNESS at top — visually climbing the ladder. - Ladder occupies left-center of content area; right side of slide is white/empty. - Bottom callout: bold indigo "Like a new hire: clear instructions, the right info, and training & checks." ### Slide 7 — Diagonal Journey Path (7 parts, 26 sessions) - A single diagonal line rising from bottom-left to top-right across most of the slide, color `#C0C0C8` (light gray), ~3–4 px thick. - Seven labeled dots on the line: - Dots 1–6: filled indigo circles (~22–26 px diameter), color `#3D3FB5`. - Dot 7 (Capstone): filled gold circle (~26 px diameter), color `#E8A020`. - Each dot has a label above/beside it: bold navy, "1 Foundations", "2 Connected", "3 Real World", "4 Senior Skills", "5 Code", "6 Production", "7 Capstone". - Bottom-left label: "YOU, today" — bold navy, below dot 1. - Top-right label: "Job-ready!" — bold gold `#E8A020`, beside dot 7. - No boxes, no background panels — path floats on white. - Slide title uses the large bold heading style; no intro sub-line used here. ### Slides 8–11 — Stacked Part-Pair Cards - **Two full-width rounded-rectangle cards** stacked vertically with ~30–40 px gap. - Card dimensions: full content width × ~160–180 px tall, ~16 px corner radius. - **Top card:** border `#3D3FB5` (indigo, ~2 px), fill white or very light lavender. - Card title: "Part N — Name (Sessions X–Y)" in Bold, ~28 px, indigo `#3D3FB5`. - "Learn:" in bold navy + plain text in regular muted gray on same line. - "Build:" in bold navy + plain text in regular muted gray on same line. - **Bottom card:** same structure. For slide 9 bottom card, border switches to gold `#E8A020` (Part 4 = Senior Skills, visually elevated). - Card title sub-format: bold "Learn:" and "Build:" keys are the same navy as body; their values are regular muted gray on the same line, differentiated only by weight. - Slide 11 has only ONE card (Part 7 is solo), centered vertically; a plain centered italic-style sentence appears below. ### Slide 12 — Portfolio Outcomes Grid + Capstone Flow - **Left zone (~60% width):** large outer rounded-rectangle container (indigo border `#3D3FB5`, ~3 px, ~16 px radius, light lavender fill or white). - Top-left badge: filled navy rectangle with "MY PORTFOLIO" in white bold ALL CAPS, ~24 px. - Inside: 3×4 grid of smaller rounded-rectangle cells (indigo border, white fill), each containing a single noun label in regular navy (~26 px): Triage, Booking, RAG, Routing, Team, Long-run, Web chat, Voice, Browser, App, LangGraph, Evals. - **Right zone (~40% width):** two horizontally connected elements: - Gold rounded-rectangle box (~200×200 px, gold border `#E8A020`, warm cream fill `#FFF5E0`): contains a large gold star icon (★, ~60 px) and "CAPSTONE" bold navy label below. - Indigo triangle arrow (`▶`) pointing right. - Indigo-bordered rounded rectangle: "Job-ready" in bold indigo ~28 px; "proof you can build" in regular muted below. - The two zones sit side-by-side with a gap; the right zone is vertically centered relative to the left. --- ## 9. Slide-Type Catalog These are the reusable layout types extracted from Session 1. Each new session should select from this catalog. ### `title` Used for: opening slide of any deck. Structure: full-width gold accent bar; centered or left-heavy large display title (ExtraBold ~96 px); gold horizontal rule below title (~3 px, ~40% width); subtitle Bold ~52 px; regular tagline ~36 px; institution / location line Regular muted; footer with "Institute · Course name". ### `closing` Used for: final slide. Structure: identical to `title` but centered vertically in content area; "Thank you!" at display scale; gold rule; bold colored sub-line ("Questions? Drop them in the chat."); regular muted tagline. Footer includes slide number. ### `bulleted-logistics` Used for: agenda, logistics, requirements, next-steps slides (slides 2, 5, 13, 14, 15). Structure: left-aligned title + gold underline rule + muted sub-heading; then 3–4 gold-dot bullet pairs (bold primary + regular muted secondary). Max 4 pairs. Max ~80 words total. ### `two-column-compare` Used for: conceptual contrast between two things (slide 3). Structure: two equal-width rounded-rect panels with contrasting fills (cream vs lavender) and contrasting border colors (gray vs indigo); ALL CAPS label at top of each; inner illustration/sub-diagram; bottom descriptor label + sub-text; bold callout sentence below both panels. ### `n-box-concept` Used for: linear process flows with N components (slide 4). Structure: N horizontally-connected rounded-rect boxes with filled arrow connectors; box labels ALL CAPS Bold; sub-label Regular muted inside; boxes use mixed border colors (indigo/gold) to denote role variation; centered caption below; bold callout analogy at bottom. ### `step-ladder` Used for: hierarchical levels or maturity models (slide 6). Structure: vertical axis arrow with "climb" / direction label; N stacked wide pill-boxes from bottom (lowest level) to top (highest level); each box: ALL CAPS label + sub-text + right-aligned step numeral; border colors escalate (gray → indigo → gold) from bottom to top; bold callout analogy below. ### `journey-path` Used for: curriculum/roadmap overview (slide 7). Structure: diagonal or curved path line on white background; labeled milestone dots at each stage; starting dot labeled "YOU, today"; final dot in gold labeled goal ("Job-ready!"); no panel backgrounds — path floats on white. Can be adapted to horizontal or arc shape. ### `part-pair-cards` Used for: curriculum part summaries in pairs (slides 8–11). Structure: 1–2 stacked full-width rounded-rect cards; each card: part title in Bold indigo (top-left, ~28 px); "Learn:" Bold + value Regular on one line; "Build:" Bold + value Regular on one line; border color = indigo for standard parts, gold for capstone/elevated parts. Card interior fill: very light lavender or white. ### `outcomes-grid` Used for: showing deliverables / portfolio items (slide 12). Structure: left zone — outer container with badge label (navy filled), inner N×M grid of item cells; right zone — capstone icon box + arrow + outcome label box. Ratio ~60/40 left/right. All borders indigo; capstone box border/fill gold. --- ## 11.
